why: Take 3 has the most life: she tries to pay a stranger from her tips, then says yes too fast and takes it back. Her fear shows in what she does, and she never has to name it. The debt-as-need premise holds to the sheet and [96030c4c4a1a18523a3fdbbb].
changes: Added a new opening line from the Fixer that uses her first name and states the payment, so the tips offer makes sense on a cold read and he is unsettling from the first word.
Cut the Bureau collector and 'late shifts': neither is on the sheet. Cut 'No, but we know you' as well, because her question about who has been asking does that work.
Rewrote his reply to the tips so he stops her because the terrace can see. She lifts 'I don't know you' from take 1, which keeps them plainly strangers.
Made the favour hint his one soft threat ('We'd only want'). Dropped to 7 beats and kept the yes-then-no and his closing line as written.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: Inez? We've just paid part of your Bureau loan.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Here, tonight's tips. I'll pay you back a little every week.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: Put those away, the terrace can see. We don't want paying.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: I don't know you. Who's been asking about me?

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: Nobody who'll trouble you. We'd only want a small favour, later.

beats.speaker: Inez
beats.line: Thank you, yes, whatever it is. No, wait, I can't, not yet.

beats.speaker: Fixer
beats.line: Say yes when you mean it. I'll be back with the rest.

learned: Inez took it; not ready yet.
